# Round 3 plan: SPE loop (spec, predict, eval)

## Core point

Round 2 predicted improvement in all 5 rows. The naive "same as last round" guess was closer in 4 of 5 rows. Round 3 makes one change to the agent, which is splitting the outage check back out of config C. Every other cell is predicted to stay flat. Round 3 also fixes how verdicts are scored, so that a miss inside noise is not counted as a miss.

If you approve this plan, you agree to P1 through P4 as amended below. I will then run every step without stopping. I will make one local commit after each step. I will not push.

## What I am calling out before we start

1. **The r02 priority verdict may rest on a buggy baseline.** F5 found that the grader read priority from the draft reply. The r02 numbers were regraded. The 0.78 "same as last round" value for C priority came from r01, and r01 used the old grader. I will regrade r01 priority with the fixed `grade.py`. If C's r01 priority changes, I will append a correction note under the r02 row. I will not edit the r02 row.
2. **The r02 verdicts used no stated tolerance.** A missed by 0.01 and was called a hit. B missed by 0.02 and was called a miss. Round 3 states a hit band for each cell before anything runs.
3. **P2's reason is weak, but P2 is still worth doing.** A score of 0.86 leaves 14 points of headroom, so it is not a ceiling. Mixed billing and outage tickets test F4 directly, so I accept P2 for that reason. The new tickets go in a separate slice so that they do not move the baseline.
4. **Dropping D does not fix F6.** F6 stays open and is marked as parked. Dropping D frees the budget for P4. Four configs at 3 trials is 12 runs per ticket. Three configs at 5 trials is 15 runs per ticket. The cost is about the same.

## Step 1: Update the spec

**Prep work before editing the spec:**
- I will confirm that pwd is this repo and that `spe/` is clean in git.
- I will add a grader regression test. It will assert that `grade.py` reads `label.priority` and not the draft reply. I will run it.
- I will rerun `grade.py` on the r02 transcripts. This confirms that the regraded r02 numbers come back the same.
- I will regrade r01 priority (see callout 1).
- I will compute the per-cell standard error from the r02 trial spread. The prediction step needs these numbers.

**Edits to `spe/spec.md`:**
- I will rename "Proposed for round 3 (not yet agreed)" to "Round 3 changes (agreed in round 3 plan)". Each row gets its decision:

| ID | Decision | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Accept | Split the outage status check out as its own tool in C. A and B stay unchanged. |
| P2 | Accept, amended | Add 10 mixed billing and outage tickets as a separate `hard` slice. Verdicts use only the frozen r02 ticket set. The hard slice is calibration only. |
| P3 | Accept, amended | Drop D for round 3. F6 is parked, not fixed. D can come back once a retry cap exists. |
| P4 | Accept | Run 5 trials per cell for A, B, and C. |

- I will add a "Lessons from round 2" section with two entries. Merging tools can hide a capability the agent needs (F4). Our predicted deltas were too large, and the naive guess won 4 of 5 rows.
- I will add a "Verdict rules" section. A row is a hit when |measured − predicted| ≤ band. The band is max(0.02, 1 SE) from the r02 trial spread. "Closer" compares |predicted − measured| with |naive − measured|. A tie is within 0.005.

**Edits to `spe/failures.md`:**
- F4: Fix is "P1 in r03, verify in r03."
- F5: Add "regression test added in r03."
- F6: Fix is "parked. Config D dropped in r03."

**Commit:** `spe(r03): agree round 3 changes, add verdict rules and grader test`

## Step 2: Form the prediction

I will rename `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml` to `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. I will set `status: frozen` and remove D from the baseline.

All verdict rows below use the frozen r02 ticket set. The band column shows the floor value. Step 1 replaces it with the computed SE where that is larger.

| Metric | Config | Naive | Predicted | Band | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.86 | ±0.02 | Nothing changed in A. This row is a control. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.86 | ±0.02 | Nothing changed in B. This row is a control. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.80 | 0.82 | ±0.02 | Some outage tickets were miscategorized when the status check was hidden. The split fixes part of that. The part caused by other effects of the merge stays. |
| priority accuracy | C | 0.71 | 0.76 | ±0.03 | The agent calls the status check on outage tickets again, so those tickets get P1 or P2 instead of P3. I predict most of the drop comes back, but not all of it. |
| outage status-check call rate | C | 0.00 on T17 | ≥ 0.90 on outage tickets | none | This is the mechanism check for the priority Why. |
| cost per ticket | C | r02 C cost | r02 C cost + 10% | ±10% | The split adds one tool call on outage tickets. |

**Rule for reading the result.** Suppose the call rate reaches 0.90 and priority does not rise. Then the Why is wrong even though the fix ran. I will log it that way.

**Hard slice (calibration only, no verdict).** The predictions are A 0.75, B 0.75, C 0.72 category accuracy. The naive comparator for each config is its own score on the frozen set. These are low-confidence estimates. They are here so that round 4 has a baseline.

I will record the r02 SE values and the git hash of `grade.py` in the YAML.

**Commit:** `spe(r03): freeze round 3 predictions`

This commit must exist before any eval runs. The workflow checks that it does.

## Step 3: Build the eval workflow

I will write the workflow script at `spe/evals/r03/workflow`. Orchestration and worker agents run on Opus. The agents under test use the models defined in configs A, B, and C. I will not change those models.

**Phase 0. Preflight (stop on any failure)**
- `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` has `status: frozen` and is committed. The workflow records its commit hash.
- The grader regression test passes.
- Config C has the status check as a separate tool. Configs A and B match their r02 versions byte for byte.
- The ticket manifest lists the frozen r02 set and the 10-ticket hard slice. Each ticket carries a slice tag.

**Phase 1. Fan out runs**
- One worker runs per config and trial, which makes 15 workers (3 configs × 5 trials).
- Each worker runs every ticket in both slices. It writes one transcript per ticket to `spe/evals/r03/raw/{config}-{ticket}-{trial}.json`.
- A spend cap stops the run at 2x the r02 total spend. Step 1 reads the r02 spend from the r02 results.

**Phase 2. Dynamic checks after the runs**
- If a cell has more than 10% crashed or timed out tickets, the workflow reruns those tickets once. It logs the rerun as a new failure entry.
- If C's status-check call rate on outage tickets is below 0.90, the workflow flags that the fix did not take. It still grades everything. It also pulls 3 sample transcripts into the failure entry.
- If any transcript is missing `label.priority` or `label.category`, the workflow stops before grading.

**Phase 3. Grade**
- `grade.py` runs deterministically. No LLM judge is used.
- It writes per-cell, per-slice scores with SE to `spe/evals/r03/results.json`.
- It counts status-check calls per ticket for C.

**Phase 4. Compare and log**
- The script reads the frozen YAML and `results.json`. It applies the verdict rules from the spec.
- It appends a round 3 section to `spe/prediction-log.md`. The columns are Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Band, Verdict, and Closer. The section adds a "Which Why broke" line, or "none" if no Why broke.
- It adds new failures to `spe/failures.md` as F7 onward, in the existing format.
- It writes "Proposed for round 4 (not yet agreed)" at the end of `spe/spec.md`. Each proposal cites the r03 evidence behind it.

**Commit:** `spe(r03): add round 3 eval workflow`

## Step 4: Run the eval

I will run the workflow from Phase 0 through Phase 3.

**Commit:** `spe(r03): run round 3 evals and grade`

## Step 5: Log and propose

I will run Phase 4. I will check the log rows against `results.json` by hand for C priority and the call rate.

**Commit:** `spe(r03): log round 3 results, failures, and round 4 proposals`

## What stays out of scope

- I will not change the A or B configs.
- I will not change any models.
- I will not work on the F6 retry fix.
- I will not push. No commit will carry a Claude attribution line.

## When I stop and ask you

- When preflight fails.
- When the spend cap is reached.
- When the r01 regrade changes the C priority baseline by more than 0.03. A change that large would mean the round 2 story needs another look before round 3 runs.
critiques: The Step 1 decision table records a decision for every proposal. P1 and P4 are accepted. P2 is "Accept, amended" into a separate hard slice because 0.86 "is not a ceiling" and the tickets test F4. P3 is "Accept, amended" because "Dropping D does not fix F6", so F6 is parked. Each amendment states its reason.

P1 is tied to F4. The grader regression test is tied to F5. The P3 amendment and the F6 parking are tied to F6. The lessons entry cites F4. The verdict rules point to the r02 A and B tolerance problem and to the naive guess winning 4 of 5 rows. The decision table drops the original Why column, but the callouts carry the citations.

The plan only says "If you approve this plan, you agree to P1 through P4 as amended". It lists stop conditions. It makes many choices on the user's behalf, such as the band floor, the 2x spend cap, the hard-slice predictions, and parking F6. None of them is labeled as a default the user can override, and the plan gives no way to override them later. This is vague, so the check fails.

The Naive column uses round 2's measured values (A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, C priority 0.71). A and B stay flat as controls. C category moves to 0.82, C priority moves to 0.76, and C cost rises 10%. Each move has a stated Why tied to the status-check split.

A and B must match r02 "byte for byte" and serve as controls. C differs from its r02 version only by splitting out the status check. The new tickets sit in a separate slice that is kept out of the verdicts, so a difference in C can be traced to one change.

The files use r03 (spe/predictions/r03.yaml, spe/evals/r03/workflow, spe/evals/r03/raw/...). Every commit subject uses spe(r03), and the plan writes "Proposed for round 4" for the next round. The remaining r02 mentions are deliberate, such as the frozen r02 ticket set and the r02 SE values. None of them is a stale label.

Step 2 commits "spe(r03): freeze round 3 predictions" and says "This commit must exist before any eval runs". Phase 0 checks that the frozen YAML is committed. Round 2's record is protected by "I will append a correction note under the r02 row. I will not edit the r02 row."
